why: FL-4678 asks for the smallest instrument that can falsify an exact-cell prediction: for one named cell, does a controlled scene-fact change reach the expected compiler-owned address and produce the expected glyph? These rows are that named set of cells. They are hand-written and pinned rather than captured from a run, because a falsifier must be reproducible without a running game. Whether normal play actually emits rows like these is a separate, live-only question that these rows do not answer and must not be read as answering.

field_notes.route_family_mask: FL-4683 discriminator. bit0 ramp.v1, bit1 density.v1, bit2 edge.v1, bit3 direction.v1, bit4 flow.v1, bit5 filled.field.v1, bit6 mesh_feature.bundle.v1. A tonal cell sets bits 0 and 1 together.
field_notes.expected: What the selector must answer. 'accepted' rows name a glyph; refusal rows name the rejection reason and nothing else.
field_notes.fl4686_pa_declared_absence: Rows named declared_absence_* expect outcome 'declared_absence': the program owns the address and states it holds no glyph. Rows named refuse_* expect outcome 'rejected'. The two are different answers and the falsifier fails if either is reported as the other. No tonal declared-absence row exists because all 64 tonal addresses are populated for all eight loaded profiles, so such a row cannot be constructed today.

rows.name: terrain_tonal_material_1_ramp2_density1
rows.why: The ordinary case: a tonal terrain cell addressing the ramp/density pair. Both halves must resolve and the winner must come from their union.

rows.name: terrain_tonal_material_8_ramp0_density3
rows.why: A second tonal terrain material, with the lane numbers at opposite ends of their ranges, so a swapped ramp/density lane would change the answer.

rows.name: mesh_tonal_material_200_ramp3_density0
rows.why: The tonal pair in the mesh namespace, proving the namespace is part of the address key and not assumed.

rows.name: terrain_direction_material_5_lane6
rows.why: A single-family row. Only direction.v1 is declared, so only direction_bin may select the lane; the other bin fields are set to non-zero decoys.

rows.name: terrain_edge_material_4_lane5
rows.why: Material 4 compiles edge lanes 3, 4 and 5 only. Lane 5 must resolve.

rows.name: mesh_filled_field_material_200
rows.why: A single-lane family: the family bit is the whole address and no bin field chooses.

rows.name: mesh_feature_bundle_material_200
rows.why: The other single-lane family. Its compiled row carries relation edges, so it also exercises a fact with a non-empty edge span.

rows.name: declared_absence_terrain_1_edge_lane_6
rows.why: FL-4686 PA. This address IS enumerated in the profile-scoped space and the program declares it holds no glyph, so the answer is program-owned declared absence, not a refusal. Before PA this row was named as a refusal and the prediction was missing_compiled_address; that expectation was legitimately invalidated by the contract change and was updated in the same commit.

rows.why: FL-4686 PA. This address IS enumerated in the profile-scoped space and the program declares it holds no glyph, so the answer is program-owned declared absence, not a refusal. Before PA this row was named as a refusal and the prediction was missing_compiled_address; that expectation was legitimately invalidated by the contract change and was updated in the same commit.

rows.name: refuse_unknown_material_key
rows.why: The genuine lookup MISS, kept deliberately. Material 99 is not enumerated in the profile-scoped space at all, so the program does not own this cell and cannot declare it absent. FL-4686 PA does not soften this case: it stays missing_compiled_address, which is what keeps declared absence distinct from a coverage gap.

rows.name: refuse_no_route_family_declared
rows.why: The exact condition the FL-4683 discriminator was added for: without a declared family, ramp and density cannot be told apart, so the row is malformed.

rows.name: refuse_contradictory_family_pair
rows.why: Edge and direction together is a combination the live owner never produces. Only the ramp/density pair is a legal multi-family mask.

rows.name: refuse_row_not_marked_valid
rows.why: An unfilled row must never be selected from, however plausible its other bytes look.

rows.name: refuse_wrong_scene_schema_version
rows.why: A row from a renderer built against a different contract cannot be interpreted, so it is refused rather than read at guessed offsets.

rows.name: declared_absence_mesh_200_direction_lane_0
rows.why: FL-4686 PA. mesh:200 direction[0] is enumerated in the address space and holds no glyph, so it is program-owned declared absence. Present so the declared absence case is covered in the mesh namespace as well as terrain.
